channel.title: Crypto Readout
channel.description: Crypto Readout reports on Bitcoin, Ethereum and altcoin markets, DeFi protocols, exchanges, stablecoins, network upgrades and crypto regulation worldwide.

item.title: What a Polygon Withdrawal Checkpoint Proves
item.description: A Polygon withdrawal checkpoint commits a range of PoS blocks to Ethereum, letting bridge contracts verify a burn before releasing the matching asset.

item.title: A bridge transfer leaves records on two chains
item.description: A bridge transfer creates evidence on two chains, and a useful tax export preserves the amounts, fees, timestamps and transaction links needed to reconcile it.

item.title: How to consolidate crypto proceeds across different chains
item.description: Consolidating crypto proceeds means choosing a destination chain, moving each asset through a route, then reconciling balances and fees before reuse.

item.title: Why Cross-Chain Swaps Can Deliver Less Than the Quote
item.description: A cross-chain quote can shrink before arrival as network costs, pool pricing, slippage and execution timing affect different parts of the swap and its payout.

item.title: Why Polygon withdrawal claims appear after the burn
item.description: Polygon PoS withdrawals burn tokens first; Ethereum releases them only after validators checkpoint the burn block and a proof is ready for a separate claim.

item.title: How Wallet-Funded Swaps Trade Without Exchange Deposits
item.description: A wallet-funded swap moves tokens from your wallet through a trading route, avoiding an exchange deposit while leaving fees, approvals and execution on-chain.

item.title: A Wallet Compatibility Check, Step by Step
item.description: A wallet compatibility check compares a wallet’s network, address, signing methods and asset support with an app’s requirements before a transaction is sent.

item.title: Impermanent Loss Comes From How Pools Rebalance
item.description: Impermanent loss is the value gap between a pool position and holding its tokens; trading fees can cover it, but only when fee income exceeds that gap.

item.title: Native coins and contract tokens do different jobs
item.description: Native coins pay a blockchain’s base fees; contract tokens follow rules set by smart contracts. Learn how balances, transfers and risks differ in practice.

item.title: SEC proposes conditional crypto custody framework
item.description: The SEC’s proposal would let advisers and regulated funds self-custody some crypto under controls, while recognizing state trust companies as custodians.

item.title: What Log Scale Shows on a Long-Run Token Chart
item.description: A log scale gives equal visual space to equal percentage moves, helping readers compare a token’s long-run path across very different price levels.

item.title: Buying Chain-Specific Coverage With XMR
item.description: Chain-specific cover follows the network or protocol named in its policy; paying in XMR is a separate step that depends on the provider’s payment rails.

item.title: How Cross-Chain Tax Recording Follows Your Crypto
item.description: Cross-chain tax records connect transactions across networks, preserve cost basis through transfers, and flag bridge fees or swaps that may count as disposals.

item.title: Why Polygon PoS Withdrawals Wait for a Checkpoint
item.description: A Polygon PoS withdrawal waits for a checkpoint to include its burn on Ethereum, then needs a separate claim transaction before the asset is released.

item.title: SEC proposes conditional self-custody for crypto advisers
item.description: The SEC has proposed a custody framework for advisers and funds that allows conditional self-custody and state trust companies, with safeguards for keys and client assets.

item.title: September crypto hacks topped $766 million, led by Bitget and Liquid
item.description: PeckShield and CertiK put September crypto thefts above $766 million, led by Bitget and Liquid Network, though much of Liquid’s bitcoin was returned.

item.title: How to Choose a Blackhole Swap Pool for Trades and Liquidity
item.description: A swap pool prices trades from token reserves, so compare depth, price impact and LP risk before choosing where to trade or add liquidity on Avalanche.

item.title: Bungee Bridge: From Approval to Destination
item.description: A bungee bridge transfer is a route across chains, not a single coin teleport: the source transaction, route and destination settlement each shape when funds arrive.

item.title: How TRON Shares Energy Between Wallets
item.description: TRON lets one account lend staked Energy to another address, so that address can run contract calls; the stake stays with its owner and fees can still apply.

item.title: How to rent TRON energy for a USDT transfer
item.description: Renting TRON energy lets a provider delegate execution capacity to your wallet, so a USDT transfer can use that resource instead of burning as much TRX.
